transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Um… yeah. I’m here because I’ve been having a really hard time with something involving my dad’s lab results. I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing people for no reason, and I know maybe it sounds like a lot, but for about the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing things or holding parts of his results back.

Doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I know I saw before. I’ve tried to let it go, I really have, but I can’t shake it, and it’s been wearing me down.

When you think about your dad's lab results being altered, does it feel like an unwanted thought that pops into your head that you wish you could stop having, or does it feel like something you're convinced is actually true and happening?

I mean… I wish I could stop thinking about it, because it’s exhausting and I know it makes me sound difficult. But it doesn’t feel like just a random thought popping in. It feels like something that’s actually happening.

I’ve tried to accept what the doctors and my family say, that the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I know I saw before. So… I guess I’m pretty convinced someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding parts back. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. It’s just been going on in my mind for about a year, and I can’t let it go.

Aside from this belief about your dad's lab results, have you noticed anything else unusual lately—like hearing voices or sounds others don't hear, seeing things others don't see, or having other beliefs that others find strange or hard to accept?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not hearing voices or seeing things, nothing like that. And I don’t really have other beliefs like this… at least not that I can think of.

It’s really just this one situation with my dad’s lab results. I know it probably sounds strange, but it feels very specific to that.
Do you have any medical conditions—like a neurological illness, head injury, or thyroid problem—or use any substances or medications that started or changed around the same time this belief began?

Um… not that I know of. I don’t have anything like that that I’ve been told about, and I can’t think of any medication or substance change that lined up with when this started.

I mean, I guess I could be forgetting something small, but nothing obvious. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Aside from this issue about your dad's lab results, how has your day-to-day life been—are you able to work, maintain relationships, and take care of your usual responsibilities normally?

I think so, yeah. I mean… outside of the whole thing with my dad’s records, I’m still functioning pretty normally.

I keep my phlebotomy shifts, I pay my bills, I take care of myself, all the usual stuff. I don’t think I’m falling apart or anything. My day-to-day responsibilities are getting done. I hope that makes sense.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion (belief that clinic staff are altering/concealing her father's lab results) present for about one year. She acknowledges the belief is distressing but is firmly convinced it is real despite contrary evidence from family and physicians, consistent with a true delusion rather than an intrusive/obsessional thought. No hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or other psychotic features are present. No mood episode symptoms (mania/depression) are reported. No medical, neurological, or substance-related etiology identified. Functioning is preserved across occupational, financial, and self-care domains outside of the delusional preoccupation. This pattern—an isolated, non-bizarre delusion of long duration with preserved functioning and absence of other psychotic or mood symptoms—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires additional symptoms and functional decline) or a brief/other psychotic disorder (duration criteria not met, and presentation is circumscribed).
